 Princeton neuroscience Ph.D. student detained by ICE
 Princeton Neuroscience Institute.
 Lousia Gheorghita / The Daily Princetonian
 Luke Grippo 
 November 19, 2026 | 10:47pm EST 
 Eva Yi Xie GS, a third-year Ph.D. student in neuroscience, has been detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement at an airport near Washington, D.C. She is believed to be held in a detention center in Chantilly, Va. Xie is the first known Princeton student to be reported to be detained by ICE.
 “The University has arranged for legal counsel to represent the student,” University spokesperson Michael Hotchkiss wrote in a statement to The Daily Princetonian Thursday night. 
 The Society for Neuroscience annual conference was held in Washington, D.C., from Saturday through Wednesday. Xie presented a poster at the conference on Wednesday titled “Entorhinal grid-like coding generalizes to jointly organize physical and cognitive dimensions.”
 Xie is a member of the Brody Lab. She is advised by neuroscience professor Carlos Brody and coadvised by neuroscience professor Nathaniel Daw and computer science professor Benjamin Eysenbach.
 “It seems wildly unfair,” Brody wrote in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ “Eva is a brilliant law-abiding student and wonderful person who has many talents to contribute to the United States. Detaining her, with the intent of deporting her, makes no sense whatsoever. It is cruel, and it is our country shooting itself in the foot.”
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Dean of the Graduate School Rodney Priestley emailed graduate students in the Princeton Neuroscience Institute about the incident at 11:01 p.m. Thursday evening. 
 “We hope she is able to soon resume her studies at Princeton,” the email, obtained by The Daily Princetonian, read. “Please be assured that we will stay in close contact with the student’s family, her legal team, and her PNI colleagues as this situation is resolved.” 
 Wynne Stagnaro GS, a fellow PNI graduate student in the Brody Lab, shared specifics of the incident in a message on the Graduate Student Government Slack. According to Stagnaro, Xie sent a “call for help” to her lab mates via Slack Thursday afternoon. She told the ‘Prince’ on Friday morning that the lab mates have been able to make contact with Xie.

 “Eva is a brilliant computational and experimental systems neuroscientist. She is also a valued colleague, mentor, and friend, and we are privileged that she chose our lab for her thesis research,” Stagnaro wrote in her message. “She went to a conference to present her work, and now she’s in a detention center. She should be home.”
 An X post from the Brody Lab shared similar sentiments.  
 Stagnaro shared that members of the Brody Lab have been in touch with the office of Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., other elected officials, and members of the media. Stagnaro did not add anything beyond the Slack post in a statement to the ‘Prince.’
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Xie is researching the “neural basis of decision-making.” She emigrated from China to the U.S. in 2016. She graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2024 with double majors in computer science and mathematics and a concentration in economics. She has interned with Meta, Microsoft AI, and IBM Research, among others. 
 At MIT, Xie was one of three undergraduates elected to the Presidential Advisory Cabinet for Institute President Sally Kornbluth and chaired the MIT Judicial Review Board. She is now on the Policy Subcommittee of the Princeton Graduate Student Committee on the Graduate School.
 Xie previously organized a workshop called “Data on the Brain & Mind” for the 2025 Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems. She is currently co-organizing the Annual Conference on Cognitive Computational Neuroscience for 2027 in Edinburgh, Scotland.

 Eysenbach and Daw could not immediately be reached for comment. ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment.
 Luke Grippo is a head News editor for the ‘Prince.’ He is from South Jersey, and typically covers the state of higher education, University affairs, and state politics. He can be reached at luke.grippo[at]dailyprincetonian.com. 
 Please send any corrections to corrections[at]dailyprincetonian.com.

 Editor’s note: This piece was updated at 11:15 p.m. on Nov. 19 to include the X post from the Brody Lab. The ‘Prince’ has received conflicting information regarding the airport where Xie was detained and has removed a reference to a specific airport. 
 Editor’s note: This piece was updated at 12:40 a.m. on Nov. 20 to include Priestley’s email, Brody’s comment, and the GSG Slack post from Stagnaro. 
 Editor’s note: This piece was updated to reflect that Xie’s lab mates were able to make contact with her after several hours of losing contact.
